edition.title: Split-Zero cohomology: moving-cutoff estimates and growing-degree arithmetic volumes
edition.scope: Polynomial source norms and quotient volumes are constructed from the completed Riemann xi function divided by the polynomial of a fixed complete zero packet. The original arithmetic convolution measure, tensor order, every zero multiplicity, total mass, coordinates, and maps into the cohomological quotient are retained. The new estimates use a cutoff following the actual equilibrium support of the Gamma reference measure and calculate the source-to-relation comparison as the admitted polynomial degree grows. The construction does not establish an off-critical zero packet or prove or disprove RH; the signed mixed-state contributions and complementary quotient returns remain open.
edition.verification_scope: The 726-page cumulative reader and 51-page proof supplement were built from the accepted complete sources. Full new proofs have written reviews at the recorded scopes. All 63 changed cumulative pages and all 51 supplement pages received layout inspection; no new review of every inherited page is claimed. The separate 562 finite algebraic and diagnostic conditions use synthetic quartets and non-interval diagnostics, not certified computation of an actual arithmetic zero packet. No new Lean execution is claimed. This is a locally assembled source edition from a result supplied as text, not a claimed producer full ZIP. Publication checks verify exact file lineage and delivered bytes; they do not replace proof review. Private conversations and correspondence are excluded from public provenance.

reader.receiver_scope: Complete proofs carry the comparison through the original coefficient maps, least-norm representatives, adjacent volume contractions, and the full four-endpoint action. They give asymptotics across the entire earlier degree band, enlarge the power-law degree range to 0<theta<d-1 with arbitrary fixed logarithmic exponent, and reach theta=d-1 with logarithmic exponent greater than one. Separate explicit coefficient enclosures apply on the stated part of the critical scale. Each result retains its full domain, arithmetic constants, multiplicities and finite guards; earlier finite estimates are intersected where both apply, without replacing their original source text.
